prerequisites: Kinematics and dynamics of point and rigid body
Newton's laws and principles of dynamic equilibrium

learning_outcomes.text: Solve complex problems autonomously within the discipline.
Draw conclusions from practical or experimental work and research carried out autonomously.
Demonstrate initiative in organizing one's own work, managing effort and time dedicated to achieving proposed objectives and goals.

syllabus_topics: Thematic Block 0: Introduction to the Machines and Mechanisms course
Thematic Block 1: Basic concepts in the theory of machines and mechanisms
Thematic Block 3: Kinematic analysis of planar mechanisms
Thematic Block 4: The dynamic problem. Force analysis.
4.3 Rigid body statics Free body diagram
4.6 Formulation of the inverse dynamic problem
Thematic Block 5: Analysis of mechanism motion
5.3 Simplified method for single DOF mechanisms
teaching_methods: Participatory master class, conferences, company visits, fair attendance, etc.
Case resolution, role-playing, technique application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.
Execution of a project to solve a problem or address a task through the planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.

Personalized and small group attention. Instruction carried out with the aim of reviewing, reorienting class materials, learning, and carrying out assignments, etc. Specific student inquiries. Scheduled tutorials.
Individual and group preparation of essays, problem solving, projects, etc. To be submitted and presented in practical classes.
Student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise elaboration, class preparation, etc.
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by weighting written tests (60%), practices/problems/questionnaires (15%), and the Integrated Project (25%). The course is considered passed if the final grade is 5 points or higher, and none of the individual part grades are below 4 points. If any written test grade is below 4 points, the final grade cannot be 4 or higher. In the second sitting, students can retake one or both written tests, or waive continuous assessment and the Integrated Project, in which case written tests will account for 100% of the final grade.
